title: AuViRe: Audio-visual Speech Representation Reconstruction for Deepfake Temporal Localization

task_scope.why_in_or_out: The paper performs temporal localization but is not conditioned on a natural-language moment query.
task_scope.transferable_value: Cross-modal reconstruction discrepancy can test query-video inconsistency or insufficient evidence.

evidence.quote: Cross-modal reconstruction is significantly more challenging in manipulated video segments, leading to amplified discrepancies, thereby providing robust discriminative cues for precise temporal forgery localization.

problem_units.micro_problem_name: Video-level deepfake classification cannot localize short manipulated segments
problem_units.micro_problem_question: How can a deepfake detector identify the exact manipulated temporal interval rather than only classify the whole video?
problem_units.failure_mode: Coarse video-level classification hides brief forged intervals.
problem_units.root_cause: Existing detectors optimize global authenticity rather than frame-level temporal boundaries.
problem_units.why_existing_methods_fail: A single video label provides no fine-grained temporal supervision or boundary prediction.

evidence.quote: Existing methods [8,9,18,19,21,25,31,34–36], primarily focus on coarse-grained video classification instead of temporal forgery localization, while neglecting to also leverage the subtle cross-modal inconsistencies that are crucial for fine-grained temporal localization.

problem_units.micro_problem_name: Multimodal deepfake detectors underuse subtle audio-visual speech inconsistencies
problem_units.micro_problem_question: How can temporal forgery localization exploit discrepancies between audio and visual speech representations?
problem_units.failure_mode: Raw-signal fusion or generic features miss subtle cross-modal speech inconsistency.
problem_units.root_cause: The relevant forgery cue is a mismatch between high-level audio and visual speech representations.
problem_units.why_existing_methods_fail: Raw audio-visual processing overfits and general-purpose encoders lack speech-specific capacity.

evidence.quote: Existing methods [8,9,18,19,21,25,31,34–36], primarily focus on coarse-grained video classification instead of temporal forgery localization, while neglecting to also leverage the subtle cross-modal inconsistencies that are crucial for fine-grained temporal localization.

method_units.macro_method_name: Reconstruction-Discrepancy Mechanisms and Evidential and Calibration Mechanisms
method_units.method_core_mechanism: Predict visual speech representations from audio and add unimodal audio-audio and visual-visual reconstruction paths.

evidence.quote: A representation reconstruction module then predicts visual speech representations from audio, complemented by unimodal (audio-audio and visual-visual) reconstructions.

method_units.macro_method_name: Reconstruction-Discrepancy Mechanisms and Evidential and Calibration Mechanisms
method_units.micro_method_name: Reconstruction-discrepancy encoding for frame-level forgery localization
method_units.method_core_mechanism: Encode cross-modal reconstruction errors as discriminative forgery cues for frame classification and temporal boundaries.
method_units.output_or_supervision: frame-level forgery scores and temporal boundaries

evidence.quote: # Abstract With the rapid advancement of sophisticated synthetic audio-visual content, e.g., for subtle malicious manipulations, ensuring the integrity of digital media has become paramount.
